newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto rival says his party heading for victory.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto rival says his party heading for victory.

text.p: Former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, rival to the ousted Benazir Bhutto, said his party was heading for a big victory in Monday's Pakistani elections.
"We are winning from all over the country," he told cheering supporters hours after the voting closed, but before any official results had been declared.
"Good news is coming from all over the country and by the morning the nation will hear very big news," he said in a brief speech outside his home in Lahore, capital of the central province of Punjab.
"This is just because of your prayers and hard work," he told his supporters.
Officials of Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party said they had received unofficial results for 75 seats of the 217-seat National Assembly (lower house) and the PML had won 73 of them.
Opinion polls had predicted that the PML would emerge as the largest party but might not win an overall majority.
